title: What is known about 1RB0RB_1RC1RA_0LD1LC_0RA1LE_1LF0LC_---1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RB_1RC1RA_0LD1LC_0RA1LE_1LF0LC_---1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the halting pattern, the left-going pass over a block and the two crossings of the block of 111110 words for every length. A halt needs a pass that reaches a lone 1 at the left end of the tape (given the observed fact that 0s inside the tape are single). After step 5,043 the next pass to reach the left end did so near step 3.3·1011, as a reduced system had predicted, and did not halt. It left 134,619 pairs 10 1110 between the old zone and a new one; passes cannot cross them, so nothing reaches the left end again until they are used up.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The halting pattern
claims.text: 0 0 1 C> 0, the pass on the separator right of a block of length 1 with two 0s on its left, halts three steps later (F reads 0). By the table this is the only way to halt (hand argument in the README).

claims.title: The pass
claims.text: Moving left from separator to separator, the pass cuts a block of length k+3 into k+1 and 1 and goes on (pass_split); a block of length 1 stops it (pass_stop). For all lengths and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: Crossing the block of words does not depend on its length
claims.text: The pass crosses n words 111110 in 6n steps, in the same state, turning each into 1110 10; the sweep back turns them into 111110 again. For every n and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: No halt in 5·10<sup>11</sup> steps; the arrivals at the left end
claims.text: The real machine runs 5·1011 steps without a halt. Passes reached the left end of the tape at triggers 1, 2, 3, 6, 27, 51 (step 5,043) and 403,962 (between steps 3.25·1011 and 3.30·1011). At the last one the 134,619 words of the block stayed behind as 1110 10 and a new zone started at the right end.

claims.title: The reduced system
claims.text: With the growing block cut to 10 words at every trigger (which, by the two crossings, should not change the rest of the tape; checked against the real machine on 20,000 triggers, not proved), the run from trigger 1,000 reaches the left end at trigger 403,962 without a halt. The real machine did the same near step 3.3·10<sup>11</sup>. Beyond that arrival the reduced run is no guide, because the block left behind is used up and its length matters.

claims.title: The leftmost zone alone
claims.text: The leftmost zone run by itself, one arriving pass at a time, from the real configuration of trigger 100, reaches the left end in tick 403,863 (trigger 403,962) with the blocks later seen in the real tape. A model, checked against the real machine at this one arrival.

claims.title: Halting needs the left end
claims.text: At the snapshots taken the 0s inside the tape are single, so the halting pattern can only form at the leftmost block. Observed, not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts if a pass reaches the leftmost block while that block is a lone 1 with blank tape on its left; nothing known forces or forbids that.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. A zone of about 120 cells is rewritten again and again by passes coming from the right, where a block of 111110 words keeps growing. The machine stops only if a pass gets through the whole zone and finds a lone 1 at the very left end of the tape. A pass got there near step 3.3·10<sup>11</sup>, as predicted, and did not stop the machine.

facts.text: The halting pattern: a pass meets a block of length 1 with two 0s on its left.
Crossing the block of words is proved not to depend on its length.
No halt; a pass reached the left end at trigger 403,962 and left 134,619 pairs that shield it.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496).
After 109 steps the tape spans 44,836 cells (21 left of the start, 32,860 right), with a density of 1s of 0.718.

sections.heading: A counter beside a growing block
html: The tape is a row of blocks of 1s with single 0s between them. At the right end a block of words 111110 grows by two cells per round trip of the head. Left of it is a zone of about a hundred cells that every round trip rewrites.

A round trip starts at the right end. The pass runs left in state C: it crosses the words (each becomes 1110 10), and in the zone it cuts every block of three or more 1s into two, until it meets a block of length 1, where it stops. The head then sweeps back, restoring the words. How deep the passes get behaves like a counter: deeper passes are rarer and rarer.

The machine halts only on 0 0 1 C> 0: the pass finds a block of length 1 with two 0s on its left. Inside the tape the 0s are single (observed), so this needs a pass that gets through the whole zone and finds a lone 1 at the very left end of the tape.

Passes reached the left end at triggers 1, 2, 3, 6, 27 and 51 (a trigger is a new cell on the right in state C), then not again until trigger 403,962, near step 3.3·1011. That arrival was predicted by two shortened runs before the real machine got there. It did not halt: the 134,619 words of the block stayed behind, and a new zone and a new block started at the right end.

Cutting the growing block short should not change the rest of the tape, because Lean proves that crossing it does not depend on its length. That reduction is checked on 20,000 triggers and at this arrival, but not proved. The stranded words are left as pairs 10 1110; a block of length 1 stops a pass, so the new zone cannot send a pass across them. It can only use them up from the right, and until all 134,619 pairs are gone nothing reaches the left end.

family: Counter zone beside a growing block of 111110 words; a halt needs a lone 1 at the left end of the tape
summary: A zone of about 120 cells is rewritten like a counter by passes coming from a growing block of 111110 words; a halt needs a pass that reaches a lone 1 at the left end of the tape. A pass reached the left end near step 3.3·10^11 without halting and left a reservoir of 134,619 pairs 10 1110 that shields the left end until it is used up (134,615 pairs left at step 5·10^11, where the run ends without a halt).
